title: decision record — extracted header of records/decisions/ADR-NNNN.md
description: ADRs stay markdown (templates/adr.md): rationale and rejected alternatives exist in no diff, and prose is their natural form. This schema binds the machine-read header lines ('Status:' / 'Date:' / 'Supersedes:' / 'Superseded-by:' / 'Amends:' / 'Amended-by:', extracted by src/records.mjs with statuses lowercased and continuation lines folded in) — the fields CTX-02/CTX-07/CTX-13 enforce semantically. Values stay free text ('none', 'ADR-0019 (D5 sizing), ADR-0017'): the storage form is what an author writes, and records.mjs' adrEdges is the one reader that turns it into edges. V1 ADR homes (docs/decisions/, docs/adr/) remain valid via decision_globs; records/decisions/ is the V2 home.

status.description: Decision state (the adr-status check's accepted vocabulary, lowercased). Superseded/deprecated require a forward link — that stays CTX-02's job.

supersedes.description: The ADR this one reverses ('none' or 'ADR-NNNN').

superseded_by.description: The ADR that reversed this one ('none' or 'ADR-NNNN') — the forward link CTX-02 requires on superseded records.

amends.description: The ADR(s) this one corrects without replacing ('none', or 'ADR-NNNN' — comma-separated, parenthesised commentary allowed). Amendment is the relation a live decision graph mostly uses: part of the amended record survives, so a reader still arrives at it. CTX-07 resolves each target; CTX-13 wants the other end to say so.

amended_by.description: The ADR(s) that corrected this one ('none' or 'ADR-NNNN') — the back-link CTX-13 requires, and the only thing that tells a reader arriving at this record that part of it has been withdrawn.
